obligation.description: For a PrepareReply emitted by handlePrepare, successful in-memory transport encoding and decoding into a fresh PrepareReply must preserve the producer accepted-value ballot for the same acceptor and instance.

scope.description: Local PrepareReply producer and lossless byte-transport contract, including nonzero accepted-value ballots.
assumptions: The receiver decodes the complete byte stream emitted by SendMsg into a fresh PrepareReply, as the normal receive loop does.
The observed producer instance is not concurrently modified during handlePrepare and byte decoding.
excluded: No quorum decision, state-machine application or end-to-end progress consequence is asserted.
No claim about startup, timer-triggered recovery, durability or crash restart.

grounding.derivation: This is a derived local implementation contract, not an imported protocol theorem: PrepareReply declares VBallot; handlePrepare copies inst.vbal into that field; SendMsg invokes Marshal and the receive loop invokes New then Unmarshal; handlePrepareReply uses VBallot to select the highest accepted-value ballot. Omitting or replacing that value changes information explicitly communicated between these callers. No field-normalization step or zero-only restriction appears in these paths. handlePropose uses owner ID as the initial ballot and handlePreAccept records it in vbal, admitting nonzero inputs.
grounding.applicability: The obligation applies independently at the producer/codec boundary. Empty reduced replicas bypass startup and workers, but normal handlers create the instance and the reply. Public codec inputs are unrestricted PrepareReply fields; no whole-cluster history premise is needed for preservation of a message produced by these handlers.
alternatives: A cluster consequence needs a separate compatible history: startRecoveryForInstance also assigns its new ballot to its local self reply, which can dominate remote evidence independently of serialization.

selections.rationale: Source shows handlePrepare exports inst.vbal and handlePrepareReply selects values by VBallot, but PrepareReply Marshal/Unmarshal omit that field. The probe produces instance contents through handlePropose, serialized PreAccept, handlePreAccept, startRecoveryForInstance and serialized Prepare before decoding the actual reply bytes. Empty bounded replica containers reproduce relevant initialization but bypass constructors, startup, dispatch, timers and execution workers; recovery is explicitly invoked rather than timer-triggered. This is a local producer/transport exploration, not a claim of quorum formation, application, safety failure or infinite stall. A later cluster consequence requires a compatible schedule and actual decision/application endpoint; recovery also relabels its local self reply with the new ballot, which may independently affect selection and must not be attributed to codec loss.

bindings.description: Serializes PrepareReply fields to the transport writer.
bindings.excerpt:
func (t *PrepareReply) Marshal(wire io.Writer) {
	var b [18]byte
	var bs []byte
	bs = b[:17]
	tmp32 := t.AcceptorId
	bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Replica
	bs[4] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[5] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[6] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[7] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Instance
	bs[8] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[9] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[10] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[11] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Ballot
	bs[12] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[13] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[14] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[15] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	bs[16] = byte(t.Status)
	wire.Write(bs)
	bs = b[:]
	alen1 := int64(len(t.Command))
	if wlen := binary.PutVarint(bs, alen1); wlen >= 0 {
		wire.Write(b[0:wlen])
	}
	for i := int64(0); i < alen1; i++ {
		t.Command[i].Marshal(wire)
	}
	bs = b[:4]
	tmp32 = t.Seq
	bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	wire.Write(bs)
	bs = b[:]
	alen2 := int64(len(t.Deps))
	if wlen := binary.PutVarint(bs, alen2); wlen >= 0 {
		wire.Write(b[0:wlen])
	}
	for i := int64(0); i < alen2; i++ {
		bs = b[:4]
		tmp32 = t.Deps[i]
		bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
		bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
		bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
		bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
		wire.Write(bs)
	}
}
